key_insight: PAIR-IBD spatially quantifies inflammation and crypt injury to distinguish pathologist-defined active ulcerative colitis from histological remission.
clinical_relevance: This ulcerative colitis study—not cancer drug discovery research—suggests AI could complement histological scoring and clinical-trial endpoint assessment, pending validation.
method: Trained a deep-learning ensemble on three IBD datasets.
Identified inflammatory cells and segmented mucosal compartments.
Quantified compartment-specific cell densities, mucin depletion and crypt architecture.
evidence_signal: In a single clinical network, active biopsies had 5.3-fold higher crypt neutrophil density than Nancy-defined remission, while key AI metrics correlated with manual scores (Spearman rs=0.50–0.73).
watch_item: Validation beyond the evaluated clinical network is needed before broader implementation; remission-like individual metrics do not establish remission in inconclusive biopsies.
paper_title: Spatial AI quantification of inflammatory and architectural features differentiates pathologist-defined active ulcerative colitis from histological remission
